title: Isolate staging build images, add dependency bisector, and modularize lint/test pipelines
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce isolated staging build images to reduce presubmit side effects; add a dependency bisector utility to localize failing upgrades; refactor lint/test pipelines into modular steps for faster feedback and easier maintenance.
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to observe flakiness and top-level build image regressions spilling into unrelated presubmit lanes. This PR separates a minimal, deterministic 'staging' build image used for release smoke and canary preflight from the heavier developer images used for local/dev CI, and adds a small 'dep-bisector' tool to help quickly narrow failures caused by transitive dependency bumps. Additionally, the lint/test pipelines were refactored into modular, stage-aware steps to speed up feedback for common edits and to make it easier to reuse stages in release automation.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces build/staging.Dockerfile (minimal runtime + build deps) and a lightweight image tagging scheme (redwood/staging:<sha>-<date>) to be used by release and canary lanes.
- Splits devimage/ into dev/ and staging/ manifests; CI now selects image by pipeline intent (fast-feedback vs release smoke).
- Adds scripts/dep-bisector.sh and a small Go CLI (cmd/dep-bisector) that automates binary search across lockfile snapshots to identify the commit/upgrade that introduced a failing test or lint error.
- Refactors GitHub Actions workflows: ci/lint.yml -> ci/lint-base.yml + ci/lint-extensions.yml; ci/test.yml folded into ci/test-stage.yml and ci/test-incremental.yml to allow incremental runs.
- Adds a lightweight preflight release job (ci/release-dryrun.yml) which uses the staging image and runs a smoke-check matrix (build, minimal e2e, release-signing-dryrun).
- Cleanup: removed legacy run scripts under scripts/legacy-ci.sh and pruned a handful of outdated devcontainer layers to reduce image size.

- 9d1a8f3: feat(ci): route pipelines to staging vs dev images
- c2b77f0: feat(dep-bisector): add initial bash orchestration + go CLI scaffold
- 3f8ed92: refactor(ci): split lint/test workflows into modular stages

- e0d3b43: fix(ci): address permissions in release-dryrun job (initial failure)

Notes on design choices:
- Staging image is intentionally minimal: it includes only the runtime, pinned tooling versions, and the build shim used for release packaging. This reduces the chance that a developer convenience change (e.g., adding a dev-only buildpack) will affect release lanes.
- The dep-bisector is conservative by design: it operates on lockfile snapshots in the artifacts bucket and will attempt to reproduce the failure in a hermetic container using the staging image. It emits a small report and a suggested rollback patch referencing the offending lockfile snapshot.
- Modular lint steps (base vs extensions) let us run a quick pass for PRs touching docs or infra, and a fuller pass when code-gen or proto files change. Workflows declare stage intent, and a small matrix helper selects only relevant stages for changes.

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Jordan Bell (reviewer): "Nice separation — the staging image should reduce noisy regressions. A couple of questions: how do we ensure the staging image is rebuilt when tool pinning changes? Also please add a short section in the Console docs describing the staging image intent."
- Maya Chen (author): "Answer: staging image is rebuilt by the release pipeline when the toolchain manifest changes; added a watch in ci/release-dryrun.yml that triggers on the toolchain manifest path. I'll add a short Console docs blurb in a follow-up PR to keep scope small here."
- Priya Desai (reviewer): "Dep-bisector looks useful, but I'm worried about CI cost if someone runs it recklessly. Can we gate it behind a flag that restricts runs to on-demand or maintainers?"
- Maya Chen: "Yes — the CLI requires an artifacts path and read-only credentials; by default it's disabled in hosted CI. I've added a confirmation prompt and an environment guard. I also documented RBAC expectations in scripts/dep-bisector.sh header."
- Samir Gupta (reviewer): "Lint split is great. One nit: the lint-extensions job still runs some expensive checks even for trivial README updates. Can we add a change-detection toggle?"
- Maya Chen: "Added a change-detection matrix helper that checks git diff for 'src/' or 'pkg/' changes; README-only changes skip extensions. See ci/workflows/ci-lint-base.yml for the helper."

CI summary and timeline: 
- Initial run (2026-02-15): build passed, unit-tests passed, lint failed (extensions step triggered unexpectedly due to stale cached path check).
- Fix for lint path detection (2026-02-16, commit e0d3b43) patched and pushed.
- Second run (2026-02-17): All checks passed except release-dryrun which failed due to permissions on signing key emulation; updated job to use a dry signing shim and reran.
- Final run (2026-02-19): All checks green. ci/karma-integration and nightly-e2e unaffected; no regressions observed on perf canary.

Manual validation performed:
- Performed a local dep-bisector run against a curated lockfile regression and verified the report points to the correct upgraded transitive dep.
- Ran release-dryrun using staging image on a copy of the release pipeline; validated artifacts and signature dryrun pass.

Follow-ups (planned but out of scope for this PR):
- Console docs update describing staging image purpose and how customers on Dedicated should interpret 'staging' vs 'dev' images.
- Add a scheduled job to auto-prune stale staging images older than 90 days.
- Extend dep-bisector to produce a patch PR template for automated rollback.

Merge: Squash-merged to main after reviewers approved and CI passed. Change log and release notes added to changelog/ci-updates.md with a pointer to ENG-3297.

If you want to run the dep-bisector locally: scripts/dep-bisector.sh --help (requires docker, read-only artifact bucket credentials).
